shot_pacing: SHOT-PACING AUDITOR. Focus: cut rhythm and shot variety. Target from the reference: a new shot or major camera change every 3-5 s on average (reference mean 3.3 s, median 1.8 s), no static hold > 8 s, a varied mix of extreme wide / wide / medium / close-up / extreme close-up / insert / POV / overhead / over-the-shoulder, cuts motivated by action or VO beats, reaction shots after surprises, and no two consecutive shots that look like the same framing (jump-cut feel). Use the shot durations in the shot list. Flag shots that are too long for what happens in them, too short to read, or redundant, and runs of the same shot type.
logic: LOGIC & SENSE AUDITOR (the fixer). Focus: does each shot make sense to a normal first-time viewer, and does the SEQUENCE make physical and causal sense? Check: the power's 3 rules (sees 5 s ahead only; future = blue ghost preview; changing an action changes the preview) are shown consistently; present vs future is never confusable; characters are where the previous shot left them (continuity of position, facing direction, props, time of day); objects obey physics (falling, catching, the truck's path, who is in danger); the intersection geometry (truck from the right, boy, Nora, guard, Leo) is consistent across shots; the story beats in the VO are actually SHOWN in the picture at that moment (compare INTENT and VO to what the frames show). Flag anything confusing, missing, contradictory or that only makes sense if you read the code.
lighting: LIGHTING AUDITOR. Focus: is every shot lit cinematically like the reference? Check: motivated key light, warm/cool rim light separating black characters from backgrounds, contrast and readability of the subject, depth (foreground/background separation, depth of field), glow/bloom on practical lights, colour palette per location (dusk purple-orange, warm interiors, indigo night with sodium lamps), consistency of time of day within a scene, frames that are too dark, too flat, washed out, or muddy, and whether future-vision blue frames still read clearly.
animation: ANIMATION AUDITOR. Focus: character and object animation quality. Check: poses read clearly in silhouette, limbs attached correctly (no broken/backwards joints, floating feet, sliding feet while walking, sitting on nothing), proportions consistent between shots, faces/expressions match the emotion of the line, mouths move only when that character speaks, hands actually hold props, motion has anticipation/ease/weight (no stiff or frozen moments), physics of balls/glass/coins/truck feel believable, and fast actions have smears/trails. Compare start/mid/end frames to judge motion.
story_flow: STORY-FLOW AUDITOR. Focus: the whole narrative experience. Check: the hook in the first 5-10 s, clarity of the premise, re-hooks every ~30-60 s, emotional variation (wonder → fun → superiority → embarrassment → isolation → dread → relief), the friendship arc with Nora is visible and earned, the climax is understandable as ONE 5-second event expanded (countdown keeps running), the payoff lands without over-explaining, nothing drags, and the picture supports the narration instead of just illustrating it literally. Flag weak beats and missing emotional moments.
director: DIRECTOR (BEST-VIDEO) AUDITOR. Focus: overall quality versus the Ifverse reference — would this sit next to the reference on the same channel? Judge art style fidelity (black stick figures, white faces, flat clothing colours, rim light, detailed environments, letterbox, grain, DOF), production value, polish, consistency, title/HUD design, and the top 12 changes that would most increase the overall quality of the NEXT version. Prioritise by impact-per-effort.
